said:
Work in Port Vesper
Port Vesper is small. People have a main profession as well as a shared duty, such as stocktaking, maintenance or emergency assistance. Their daily work continues while the player investigates.
Begin with eight important professional roles. A small unnamed support team keeps the port and essential services running; these people do not all need to be simulated individually.
| Profession or role | Daily work | Usual workplace | Significance for the player |
| Port Coordinator | Arrange arrivals, cargo, supplies, lodging and departure windows. | Arrival Lock; administration in Commons. | Knows who arrived, what is missing and when transport is possible. |
| Research Lead | Compare signal data, distribute research tasks and prepare the expedition. | Orison Listening Room; briefings on Common Deck. | The client; assesses research and grants access to the Peregrine. |
| Chief Engineer | Test the experimental drive, investigate defects and uphold safety limits. | Workshop and Peregrine Hangar. | Can repair equipment, share technical knowledge and declare departure unsafe. |
| Signal Technician | Calibrate antennas, check recordings and locate faults. | Orison Listening Room; travelling via Ridge Shelter. | Knows the original measurements and maintenance history. |
| Pilot-Navigator | Prepare routes, fuel, manoeuvres and abort procedures; practise in simulations. | Peregrine — Common Deck. | Assesses whether a proposed journey is feasible. |
| Field Mechanic | Maintain external pipes, relays, doors and vehicles. | Workshop and Coastal Traverse. | Knows the route to Orison Ridge and can accompany you as a guide or repairer. |
| Medic | Provide consultations and care for supplies, continuity implants and the recovery cradle. | Medical Bay. | Treats injuries and determines whether someone is medically fit for fieldwork or departure. |
| Steward | Cook, care for sleeping quarters and track water and food supplies. | Commons and Guest Quarters. | Hears a great deal without knowing everything; notices who skips meals or fails to return. |

The research lead may propose departure, but a regular launch requires the chief engineer's, pilot's and medic's agreement. These responsibilities are known in advance and do not depend on whom the player likes best.
Daily rhythm
Port Vesper uses a standard 24-hour day. Rosters and terminals display exact times. In conversation, people usually say “after breakfast”, “before evening handover” or “when the night watch comes on”.
| Time | Ordinary daily rhythm |
| 06:30–07:30 | Breakfast in Commons; the first shift receives its handover. |
| 07:30–12:00 | First work period. Field teams check the weather and equipment before departure. |
| 12:00–13:00 | Midday meal, staggered to keep essential posts staffed. |
| 13:00–17:30 | Second work period: maintenance, research, training and resupply. |
| 17:30–18:00 | Finish work, return tools and report anything noteworthy. |
| 18:00–19:00 | Evening meal in Commons. A good time to meet several people. |
| 19:00–22:00 | Free time, personal projects, conversations and sometimes research. |
| 22:00–06:30 | Sleep for the ordinary day shift. |

Travel time counts. Someone leaving Commons for Orison at 07:30 begins work there at around 08:04 in normal weather, rather than being in both places at once.
Different schedules
| Role | Particular rhythm |
| Port Coordinator | Usually 07:00–16:00. A late landing shifts the duty period; a harbour watch officer takes over the counter. |
| Research Lead | Usually 09:00–18:00. Alternates days at the listening station with analysis and meetings in the settlement. |
| Chief Engineer | Usually 08:00–17:30. A late test requires compensatory rest the next day. |
| Signal Technician | Early field shift: departure around 07:30, back before the evening meal. Night recordings are automatic. |
| Pilot-Navigator | Usually 09:00–18:00, with scheduled exercises. Rest is mandatory before departure. |
| Field Mechanic | Usually 07:30–16:30. Outdoor work is rescheduled in dangerous weather; indoor repairs then take priority. |
| Medic | Consultations 08:00–12:00 and 14:00–17:00. Available for emergencies outside those hours, with a trained first aider on watch. |
| Steward | An early shift for breakfast and lunch, a long afternoon break and a short evening period. Other residents wash up and tidy according to a roster. |

Night watch and safety
The support team divides port and systems watch into three eight-hour shifts: 06:00–14:00, 14:00–22:00 and 22:00–06:00. The watch monitors pressure, fire alarms, distress calls and arrivals. It is not an all-knowing surveillance service.
Orison Ridge is normally unmanned at night. Equipment continues recording. A fault is noticed only when a sensor or connection actually reports it. Researchers may schedule a night observation, with an agreed check-in time.
The medic and chief engineer may be woken for a genuine emergency. This costs them sleep and affects their availability the next day. For an ordinary question, the watch may advise waiting until morning.
Restday
On Restday, most routine duties are suspended. Meals, emergency medical care, life support and harbour watch remain available. People do personal maintenance, visit one another or remember someone.
Research may continue if there is a clear reason, but not everyone automatically gives up their day off.
Aboard the Peregrine
Of the eight roles, the research lead, chief engineer, pilot and medic initially travel aboard. Including the player, that makes five people. The sixth place may later be assigned to the signal technician or field mechanic, depending on the expedition's established needs.
During quiet flight, automatic control monitors the ship. A rested crew member stands watch according to the roster. Critical manoeuvres require several qualified people; the player is not made responsible for piloting without training.
For the Chronicler
A schedule describes what someone intends to do. Appointments, danger, illness and resources determine whether it succeeds. Let characters interrupt their work when there is a reason, and say when they need to return to it.
Waiting must be an understandable choice. Someone who misses a person can ask when they are expected back, leave a message or make an appointment. Do not constantly repeat eating, walking and sleeping notifications; show daily routines mainly when they tell the player something or offer an opportunity.
